lower_bounds: G >= max_i(n_i), because one bank contributes at most once per group
G >= ceil(sum_i(n_i)/K), because a group carries at most K sources
scheduler_theorem.sufficiency_induction: Let G=max(M,ceil(T/K)). Greedy decrements the min(K,p) largest positive banks. The new total is <=K(G-1): for p>=K this follows from T<=KG; for p<K, T<=pG and all p banks are decremented. The new maximum is <=G-1: if any unselected bank had G, at least K+1 banks had G, contradicting T<=KG. Thus the bound drops by one each round; greedy finishes in at most G rounds, while the two lower bounds require at least G.
